newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: GOLF-MCNULTY WINS BY FOUR STROKES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MCNULTY WINS BY FOUR STROKES.

text.p: Mark McNulty preserved his four-shot overnight margin to win the 400,000 rand (56,000 pounds) Zimbabwean Open from former world number one Nick Price and South African Justin Hobday on Sunday.
The 43-year-old Zimbabwean won for the second time with a closing 69 at the Chapman Golf Club for a 72-hole total of 270, 18-under-par.
Price, who struggled all week with his putting, carded a closing 68 to share second place with Hobday on 274.

"My biggest problem this week has been reading the greens," Price said. ".My first six putts today were all good ones and I didn't make one. I could have been five-under after the first seven holes the way I was playing but I just couldn't get close to Mark to apply the pressure."

Hobday returned the low round of the day with five birdies in a tidy 67 but, having got to 13-under at the 11th, he was unable to apply any further pressure on McNulty until, too late, he birdied the last.
McNulty's victory was his fourth of the year, after European tour wins in the Dimension-Data tournament in South Africa, the Dutch Open and the prestigious Volvo Masters in Valderrama.
"It's always nice to win four in a year and obviously it's a great feeling to win here in Zimbabwe again," McNulty said.
"And it's especially great to be able to give it back to the people here who support me and Nick (Price) all year round by following our progress on television and in the newspapers."
McNulty never allowed his closest challengers to get closer that four behind.
The 1992 winner began in the best possible way with a birdie three at the first to stretch his lead to five shots.
The outcome was probably decided at the 400-yard third. Price, five behind overnight, had a good chance of gaining a two-shot swing at that hole - and also to get his own round kick-started.
McNulty's approach went over the green and he ran up a bogey five but Price, who had hit his second to three feet, missed his birdie attempt.

Despite playing solidly from tee to green, Price could barely make a putt on the front nine. Out in 35, with an overdue birdie at the par-five ninth, he came back in 33 with birdies at the 10th and 13th and an eagle three at the 18th to draw level with Hobday at 14-under.
